headline: New half-marathon block starts today, but the composite verdict reads red — treat this 7K as genuinely easy, not another grey-zone day.
body_state: Garmin readiness is 52, the composite score 60.4 (moderate, driver: sleep) — but the overall verdict flags **red**: acute:chronic load ratio 1.60 (>1.5 = 2–4x injury risk next week) and 26h of accumulating 14-day sleep debt. Last night was only 6.3h (score 66, deep 32%, REM just 4.7%). HRV is BALANCED (45ms) and body battery recharged well overnight (+44 to 47), stress is low (avg 15) — the recovery signals are fine, it's the load and sleep ledgers that aren't. TSB sits at -13.2, still inside the -5…-30 productive zone, and training status reads "Recovery." Load focus is skewed anaerobic.
session: **7km Easy Run** @ 4:50–5:19/km — week 1 of the new Half Marathon plan (target Sep 21). Given the ACWR spike, run the slow end of that window, not the fast end: yesterday's "easy" 5K sat at 89.7% zone-3 time (4:27/km, HR 136 vs an LTHR of 163), which is exactly the grey-zone pattern the plan is flagging. Cap HR around 115–130, hold conversational pace, and use the first 10 minutes to lift cadence toward 165–170 spm before letting stride open up.
recent: Aug 10's easy 5K ran fast-for-easy (4:27/km, HR136, 89.7% zone-3) — turnover-driven, not overstriding, but still moderate effort under an "easy" label. The new plan (created Aug 10) resets the block at week 1, but the same grey-zone habit that flattened last week is still showing up day one.
focus: Keep today's run genuinely easy — HR 115–130, not the 4:2X/km pace the last few "easy" days have drifted to.
ACWR is 1.60 (high flag) — don't add anything unplanned this week; let the plan's own volume do the work.
